citation: DeBellis, Storer, Harvey, Beane, Edwards, Fraser, Good, Kalliamvakou, Kim, Maxwell, D'Angelo, Inman, Murillo, Villalba. DORA 2025 State of AI-assisted Software Development Report. DORA / Google Cloud, 24 September 2025. https://dora.dev/dora-report-2025/ ; https://research.google/pubs/dora-2025-state-of-ai-assisted-software-development-report/
source_tier: Company research (Google Cloud DORA programme, annual survey-based report)
access_status: Landing pages, Google Research abstract and Google Cloud announcement blog read. Full report PDF NOT opened [uncertain]
sponsor_and_incentive: Presented by Google Cloud, which sells AI tooling (Gemini, Cloud). Research partners listed on dora.dev: IT Revolution (Premier), GitHub, GitLab, SkillBench, Workhelix. Several partners sell AI developer tools.
exact_quotes: "AI's primary role is as an amplifier, magnifying an organization's existing strengths and weaknesses." (dora.dev report landing page)
"AI's primary role in software development is that of an amplifier." (Google Research abstract)
"AI doesn't fix a team; it amplifies what's already there." (Google Cloud announcement blog, key takeaway)
date_and_recency: Published 24 September 2025 (per Google Cloud blog). Data collection window not confirmed from pages opened [uncertain].
key_claims: AI acts as an amplifier of existing organizational strengths and weaknesses. Greatest returns come from the organizational system (the seven-capability DORA AI Capabilities Model), not the tools. AI adoption now positively relates to delivery throughput and product performance (a change from 2024) but still negatively to delivery stability, attributed to larger change volume exposing weak downstream controls such as automated testing, version control and fast feedback loops. Seven team archetypes identified by cluster analysis of performance, stability and well-being.
headline_figures: Nearly 5,000 technology professionals surveyed plus 100+ hours of qualitative data (exact n of 4,867 recalled from the report but not confirmed on pages opened) [uncertain]. 90% report using AI at work. More than 80% believe AI increased their productivity. 30% report little or no trust in AI-generated code, slightly lower than last year. 90% of organizations have adopted at least one internal platform. Seven team archetypes. Seven capabilities in the AI Capabilities Model.
sample_unit_and_population: Individual technology professionals worldwide (survey), plus 100+ hours of qualitative interviews. Mixed organization sizes; not open-source specific. Exact n 4,867 [uncertain].
observed_vs_stated: Mostly self-reported survey responses (trust, productivity belief, usage). Throughput and stability are also survey-derived measures, not telemetry [uncertain, not confirmed in full report].
what_makes_trust_justified: The report points to organizational capabilities rather than individual trust: from memory of the report, the seven capabilities are a clear and communicated AI stance, healthy data ecosystems, AI-accessible internal data, strong version control practices, working in small batches, user-centric focus, and quality internal platforms [uncertain, list not verified from opened source]. Blog confirms automated testing, version control and fast feedback loops as the controls that limit instability.
what_it_costs: Not quantified in the pages opened. Implied cost is investment in platform, testing and small-batch discipline rather than reviewer time [uncertain].
failure_mode_class: Over-reliance and instability: more change volume exposes weak downstream controls, lowering delivery stability.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Controls named: automated testing, strong version control, fast feedback loops, small batches.
limitations_stated: No limitations text found on pages opened; the blog uses 'relationship', i.e. correlational language. Full-report limitations section not read [uncertain].
counter_evidence: Report itself finds AI adoption still associated with worse delivery stability. 30% distrust code yet 90% use AI. Sponsor is an AI vendor, and survey self-report may overstate productivity (METR RCT found experienced developers slower, from general knowledge, not from this source) [uncertain].
verification_status: Verified against opened pages: publication date, 90% usage, 80% productivity, 30% little/no trust, amplifier quotes, throughput/stability direction, 'nearly 5,000'. NOT verified: n=4,867, '24% highly trust' recalled figure, seven capability names, survey window, limitations. [uncertain]
usable_claim: DORA's 2025 report, a Google Cloud survey of nearly 5,000 technology professionals, found about 30% had little or no trust in AI-generated code even though about 90% use AI at work, and that AI adoption still correlated with lower delivery stability, which the authors tie to weak testing, version control and feedback loops.
do_not_use: The 4,867 figure, the '24% highly trust' figure and the list of seven capabilities until checked in the full PDF. Do not present correlations as causal or the survey as observed behaviour.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays [uncertain].
